hints: Let H be female student height: H ~ N(mu, sigma^2).
Two percentiles are given: P(H < 182.7) = 0.90 and P(H < 162.5) = 0.40.
Find the critical values: For 0.90, z1 = 1.282. For 0.40, lower tail gives Phi(-z) = 0.40 => Phi(z) = 0.60, so z2 = -0.253.
Set up two equations: (182.7 - mu) / sigma = 1.282 and (162.5 - mu) / sigma = -0.253.
Subtract equations: 182.7 - 162.5 = [1.282 - (-0.253)] * sigma => 20.2 = 1.535 * sigma, so sigma = 13.2.
walkthrough:
Translate the two given probabilities into standard normal $z$-scores for $H \sim \operatorname{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$:
- $P(H < 182.7) = 0.90 \implies z_1 = 1.282$
- $P(H < 162.5) = 0.40 \implies \Phi(-z_2) = 0.40 \implies \Phi(z_2) = 0.60 \implies z_2 = -0.253$

Set up the system of simultaneous standardisation equations:
$$\frac{182.7 - \mu}{\sigma} = 1.282 \implies 182.7 - \mu = 1.282\sigma \quad \text{(1)}$$
$$\frac{162.5 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.253 \implies 162.5 - \mu = -0.253\sigma \quad \text{(2)}$$

Subtract equation (2) from equation (1) to eliminate $\mu$ and solve for $\sigma$:
$$182.7 - 162.5 = 1.282\sigma - (-0.253\sigma)$$
$$20.2 = 1.535\sigma \implies \sigma = \frac{20.2}{1.535} \approx 13.1596 \approx 13.2\text{ cm}$$
$$(13.1 \le \sigma \le 13.2)$$

Substitute $\sigma$ back into equation (1) or (2) to solve for $\mu$:
$$\mu = 162.5 + (0.253 \times 13.1596) = 162.5 + 3.3294 = 165.829 \approx 166\text{ cm}$$
$$(165.8 \le \mu \le 166)$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up the model and percentile conditions:
Let $H$ be the height of a female student at Breven college:
$$H \sim \operatorname{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$$
We are given:
1. $P(H < 182.7) = 0.90$
2. $P(H < 162.5) = 0.40$

Step 2: Obtain the corresponding z-values:
- From the percentage points table, for upper probability $0.90$:
$$z_1 = 1.282$$
- For lower probability $0.40$ (which is less than $0.5$, so $z$ is negative):
$$\Phi(-z_2) = 0.40 \implies \Phi(z_2) = 0.60$$
From the normal distribution table, $\Phi(0.25) = 0.5987, \text{ diff for } 3 = 11 \implies \Phi(0.253) = 0.5998 \approx 0.60$:
$$z_2 = -0.253$$

Step 3: Write down the two linear equations:
$$\frac{182.7 - \mu}{\sigma} = 1.282 \implies 182.7 = \mu + 1.282\sigma \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$
$$\frac{162.5 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.253 \implies 162.5 = \mu - 0.253\sigma \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Step 4: Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1 to find sigma:
$$182.7 - 162.5 = (\mu + 1.282\sigma) - (\mu - 0.253\sigma)$$
$$20.2 = 1.535\sigma$$
$$\sigma = \frac{20.2}{1.535} = 13.1596... \approx 13.2\text{ cm}$$

Step 5: Solve for mu:
$$\mu = 182.7 - 1.282(13.1596) = 182.7 - 16.8706 = 165.829... \approx 165.8\text{ cm} \text{ (or } 166\text{ cm)}$$
Thus, $\mu = 166\text{ cm}$ (or $165.8\text{ cm}$) and $\sigma = 13.2\text{ cm}$.

hints: From the stem, P(height < 162.5) = 0.40, so P(height > 162.5) = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60.
In a sample of 10 students, let X be the number with height > 162.5 cm: X ~ B(10, 0.6).
Fewer than 8 means X <= 7, which is easiest via complement: 1 - [P(X = 8) + P(X = 9) + P(X = 10)].
walkthrough:
Find the probability that a student has height greater than $162.5\text{ cm}$:
$$P(H > 162.5) = 1 - P(H < 162.5) = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60$$
$$X \sim \operatorname{B}(10, 0.6)$$

Express 'fewer than 8' using the complement of the upper tail:
$$P(X < 8) = P(X \le 7) = 1 - [P(X = 8) + P(X = 9) + P(X = 10)]$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the single-trial probability:
From the problem stem, the probability that a female student has a height less than $162.5\text{ cm}$ is $0.40$.
Therefore, the probability that a student has a height greater than $162.5\text{ cm}$ is the complement:
$$p = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60$$
and $q = 1 - p = 0.40$.

Step 2: Model the sample as a Binomial random variable:
For $n = 10$ randomly chosen students, let $X$ be the number with height $> 162.5\text{ cm}$:
$$X \sim \operatorname{B}(n, p) = \operatorname{B}(10, 0.6)$$

Step 3: Express fewer than 8 using the complement rule:
$$P(X < 8) = P(X \le 7) = 1 - P(X \ge 8) = 1 - [P(X = 8) + P(X = 9) + P(X = 10)]$$
